title: Mrs. Brown on her husband's bands
summary: Mrs. Raymond Brown recalls the bands her husband played in and musicians who played with him, including the Texas band and Pichon's.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: There's anything you can tell us about Mr. Brown or?
No, Harold and she know everything about Brown because she know all the musicians during them time.
Yeah, we can actually do that.
And all that. Come tell them about all the fellas used to come at the house, what they used to do.
We used to sleep there for days and a days out.
Yeah.

Well, just a little bit about your husband if you don't mind. Tell us a little bit about him. I'm Bill Russell. I work at Tulane University. We collect the material for Tulane in the library to try and preserve this old history, you know, about the musicians. You want to sit down there a minute?
Who used to play with him, huh?
Who used to play with him during that time? Like Sean and John McCullough.
Sean McCullough. Sean McCullough. Who used to do? And a little bit of, I don't even know how old he was or just when did he die. I never didn't hear him or meet him of course, so. I'm saying.

He's been there about 25 years. Quite a long time ago. 25 years. Yeah, about 25 years. Oh, I can't. I wish I had a new job coming here for that for I could be thinking of them. When Chris was here, she could remember all of them names. Well, what do you remember? Do you remember some places he played? Oh, well at that time they played out at the country clubs. They all closed up out there on the highway now.
Like on Jefferson, down in Jefferson. Yeah, okay. Beverly was the one of those days. Beverly was the one of those days.

Oh, and you want to think of something you can't. You can't think all the names of them places. I can't remember the days. There was a band that he played with besides the Desdune band. Some of the bands he played with. I don't know. Was that Desdune died, Angel? Yeah, Desdune died. Desdune died, yeah. And he played, well, all I can remember is playing with him out in Texas. Well, he was with honeycomb, the tenor player was his band. That's his brother, Matt Brown. Yeah, his brother. Mr. Steevio's band. I mean, my daughter, she can remember way back, right? I done forgot all them boys' names. Used to be home all the time. Well, how about Clifford? When Clifford boys started playing trumpet, do you remember that? Yeah, he started when he was about, he started when about 16. Yeah. Just about 16. Because he played on, I don't know what, I don't forgot what bands he played with. I know the last band he played with was on Sting or Captain. Do you know what band that was?
Yeah, Pishon's band.
Pishon's band. He played from here to New York and then finally stayed in New York. So I never could keep up with him no more in the bands.
But you don't remember about Shine and Walter that died.
Yeah, Shine can remember Shine and...
Gopher played the piano.

What about the only two I do remember? Gopher on piano. I just don't know how some time if we really had to go home. And another young boy coming out of the game on that other boy, Kobe, what was his name? Kobe, George Kobe. Yeah, George Kobe. Yeah, George Kobe and...
George McAuliffe.
And George McAuliffe. And what you calling Alvin? Alvin, Alvin, Alvin.
Yeah, Alvin.

Alvin, Alvin. Related to Cullen. Well Alvin took his place in the band when he had to come back home. His wife was going to have a good boy to a child. Alvin came to medicine somewhere in Nebraska. That's another one. Benny. Another boy, Benny, he's dead. Benny Turner. Benny Turner's not dead at all. You know Ben? He's a pianist? He's over and out there. Oh no, I know. Not a band. Yeah, I know. He's a dog, dog, prostitute. Yeah, I know Ben. Sure, I know Ben.
Is he a pianist too? Yeah, he's a pianist.
Now, that's not all I can remember. After y'all gone, then I'll remember home.
